q: When you meet confusion and disappointment in your faith, are you willing to bring them to God and seek His guidance and revelation? How can you keep your faith in God in hardship?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for walking with us even when we are confused and disappointed. Help us, on the journey of faith, to learn to bring all our questions and confusion to You, seeking Your wisdom and revelation. May we understand and obey Your purpose more fully. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He said to them, “Foolish men, and slow of heart to believe in all that the prophets have spoken!
Didn’t the Christ have to suffer these things and to enter into his glory?”
Beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, he explained to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.
b: This passage records how Jesus opened the disciples' minds to understand the prophecies in the Scriptures. When the disciples were confused about Jesus' death, He rebuked them for their foolishness and slowness of heart, and explained that His suffering and resurrection were part of God's plan of salvation. Beginning with Moses and all the prophets, He explained to them the prophecies in the Scriptures, so that they would understand that everything was in God's hands and was for the fulfillment of His plan.

This passage reminds us that God's word is full of revelation for our lives, yet we often overlook it because of dullness of heart or ignorance of God's word. Jesus' explanation gave the disciples a fresh understanding of the truth of Scripture, which tells us that in difficulty we should ask God to open our hearts so that we can understand His word more deeply.

Through this passage God tells us that His word is the light that guides us through hardship. We need to let God's word take root in our hearts and meditate on it often, so that we can better understand God's plan and purpose in our lives.
q: Do you often meditate on God's word and ask Him to open your heart so that you understand His plan more fully? How can you rely more on the teaching of Scripture in daily life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us the Bible as a guide for our lives. Help us to meditate on Your word often and let Your truth take root in our hearts. When we feel confused or lost, may Your Holy Spirit enlighten us so that we can understand and obey Your purpose. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: They came near to the village where they were going, and he acted like he would go further.
They urged him, saying, “Stay with us, for it is almost evening, and the day is almost over.” He went in to stay with them.
When he had sat down at the table with them, he took the bread and gave thanks. Breaking it, he gave it to them.
Their eyes were opened and they recognized him, then he vanished out of their sight.
b: This passage describes the evening meal that Jesus shared with the two disciples in the village of Emmaus. When they urged Him to stay, Jesus accepted their invitation and, at the table, broke bread with them. At the moment He broke the bread, the disciples' eyes were opened and they recognized Him. In that moment they finally understood that the one who had been walking with them was the risen Jesus.

This passage reminds us that God's presence often appears in our everyday lives, and when we invite Him into our lives, He reveals Himself to us. The disciples recognized Jesus as they shared bread with Him, which shows that in intimate fellowship with God we can know Him more deeply and experience spiritual awakening in His presence.

Through this passage God tells us that He wants to be with us at every moment of our lives. We need to learn, like these two disciples, to invite Jesus into our lives and share our daily lives with Him, so that our eyes will be opened and we will recognize His presence.
q: How do you invite Jesus into your daily life and have fellowship with Him? How can you come to know Him better through that fellowship?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for being with us at every moment of our lives. Help us to invite Jesus into our lives often and to know Him more deeply in fellowship with Him. May our eyes be opened to see Your wonderful works. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: They said to one another, “Weren’t our hearts burning within us, while he spoke to us along the way, and while he opened the Scriptures to us?”
They rose up that very hour, returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and those who were with them,
saying, “The Lord is risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon!”
They related the things that happened along the way, and how he was recognized by them in the breaking of the bread.
b: This passage records how the two disciples, after recognizing Jesus, with burning hearts returned at once to Jerusalem to share their experience with the other apostles. That burning in their hearts symbolizes the spiritual renewal and encouragement that came from Jesus' presence and words. They could hardly wait to tell others the good news that Jesus had risen, and their enthusiasm reflects the revival of their faith.

This passage reminds us that when we experience God's real presence and the power of His word, our hearts are stirred and we long to share that joy with others. Jesus' resurrection is not only a historical event but our hope and strength for every day, and like these disciples, we should pass this good news on to those around us.

Through this passage God tells us that when we meet Him, our lives are renewed and our hearts are set on fire. Let us pass on this joy and love that come from God, be a blessing to others, and bear witness to His wonderful works.
q: When you experience God's presence and the power of His word, does your heart burn within you? How will you share that joy with others and be a blessing to them?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for letting us experience the power of Jesus' resurrection, which sets our hearts on fire and fills them with Your love and joy. Help us to pass this joy on to those around us, to be a blessing to them, and to bear witness to Your wonderful works. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: As they said these things, Jesus himself stood among them, and said to them, “Peace be to you.”
But they were terrified and filled with fear, and supposed that they had seen a spirit.
He said to them, “Why are you troubled? Why do doubts arise in your hearts?
See my hands and my feet, that it is truly me. Touch me and see, for a spirit doesn’t have flesh and bones, as you see that I have.”
When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.
While they still didn’t believe for joy, and wondered, he said to them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”
They gave him a piece of a broiled fish and some honeycomb.
He took them, and ate in front of them.
b: This passage records Jesus appearing to His disciples after His resurrection. The disciples at first were startled and doubtful, unable to believe that what they saw was the real Jesus. Jesus knew their confusion, so He showed them His hands and feet and even ate food with them, to prove that His resurrection was real and not a hallucination. This not only comforted the disciples but also strengthened their faith in the resurrection.

This passage reminds us that Jesus' resurrection is real; it is not merely a spiritual experience but a bodily resurrection. When we feel confused or doubtful in our faith, we should, like the disciples, bring it to Jesus, and He will comfort us in His own way, strengthen our faith, and help us understand more deeply the power of His resurrection.

Through this passage God tells us that His presence is real and that Jesus' resurrection gives us the hope of eternal life. Let us hold fast to this faith and continue to experience His presence and guidance in our lives.
q: When you meet confusion or doubt in your faith, how do you respond? How do you continue to experience the power and presence of Jesus' resurrection in daily life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us the hope of eternal life through the resurrection of Jesus Christ. Help us to keep a firm faith, and whenever we meet confusion or doubt, to depend on Your guidance and experience Your real presence. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He said to them, “This is what I told you, while I was still with you, that all things which are written in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms, concerning me must be fulfilled.”
Then he opened their minds, that they might understand the Scriptures.
He said to them, “Thus it is written, and thus it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead the third day,
and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name to all the nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
You are witnesses of these things.
Behold, I send out the promise of my Father on you. But wait in the city of Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from on high.”
b: This passage records the scene in which Jesus, after His resurrection, explained the Scriptures to His disciples and entrusted them with a mission. Jesus opened their minds so that they could understand everything in the Scriptures written about Him, and He gave them the task of proclaiming the gospel, making them witnesses of His resurrection. He also promised the coming of the Holy Spirit, who would clothe them with power to fulfill this important mission.

This passage reminds us that God's Word is the vital way to understand His will. We need to ask God to open our minds so that we may know His plans and purposes more deeply. Jesus also gives us the Holy Spirit to help us and empower us to witness to His love and salvation. This is the mission every Christian is called to carry.

Through this passage God tells us that His Word is truth. We should keep seeking His will in the Scriptures and put His teaching into practice in our daily lives. We must also rely on the power of the Holy Spirit to proclaim the gospel boldly and become His witnesses.
q: When you read the Bible, do you ask God to open your mind so that you can understand His Word more deeply? How do you put these truths into practice in your life and boldly witness to Jesus' salvation?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us the Bible as our guide, and for giving us the Holy Spirit to empower us to proclaim Your truth. Help us to witness boldly to Your love in our daily lives and to carry out Your will with obedient hearts. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He led them out as far as Bethany, and he lifted up his hands, and blessed them.
While he blessed them, he withdrew from them, and was carried up into heaven.
They worshiped him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
and were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.
b: In this passage we witness Jesus' ascension after His resurrection. Jesus led the disciples out as far as Bethany, lifted up His hands, and blessed them. This act of blessing was full of warmth and love, showing Jesus' deep care for His disciples and the trust He placed in them. Then He was carried up into heaven before their eyes, the glorious return to heaven after finishing His work on earth.

After witnessing this holy moment, the disciples were not saddened by the parting. Instead, their hearts were filled with joy as they returned to Jerusalem. They were continually in the temple, praising God, which shows the faith and hope they received through Jesus' resurrection and ascension. They understood that although Jesus no longer lived among them on earth, His Spirit and His promises would be with them forever.

Through this passage God reminds us that Jesus' ascension is not an ending but a new beginning. His blessing and His Spirit remain with us, and whatever circumstances we face, we can be filled with joy and hope as we trust in Him. Like the disciples, we should praise God continually and welcome each day with a joyful heart.
q: How do you experience the presence of Jesus in your life? Are you willing to keep your faith and joy even in difficulty?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us Jesus Christ. His ascension helps us understand that He is with us always. Help us to praise You continually and to face every challenge with faith and joy. May our lives be filled with hope because of Jesus' presence. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
The same was in the beginning with God.
All things were made through him. Without him, nothing was made that has been made.
In him was life, and the life was the light of men.
The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn’t overcome  it.
b: In this passage John takes us back to the eternal beginning and shows us the true nature of Jesus. He did not begin to exist in Bethlehem, nor did He first appear in a manger. In the beginning He was already with God the Father; He is God Himself, the eternal Word. All things were made through Him, and the order of the whole universe and the origin of life come from Him.

The passage says, “In him was life, and the life was the light of men.” Jesus did not come to improve our lives; He came to be our life. He does not merely tell us where the light is; He Himself is the light, shining into the deepest part of our hearts so that we may see the truth, our direction, and the way. When His light shines in, the hidden self, pride, fear, and confusion within a person are exposed, so that we can be renewed.

Yet the darkness did not receive the light. This reminds us that the problem is often not that the light is too weak, but that the human heart is unwilling to submit, unwilling to give up its own sovereignty, unwilling to let God rule. But when we humble ourselves, open our hearts, make room, and let Jesus be King within us, His light drives out the darkness, truth guides our steps, and life is restored to order.

Jesus came so that we would no longer live by ourselves but let Him live in us; no longer analyze with our minds but obey the Holy Spirit's prompting from the heart; no longer be our own master but let God be glorified in us.
q: Are there corners of your heart that are still in darkness? Will you let the light of Jesus enter them today and bring renewal and freedom?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for sending Jesus to be the light of life and to shine on our darkness. Help us to open the doors of our hearts, not to resist Your truth, and not to rule ourselves as king, but to let Jesus reign within us. May Your light guide our steps every day. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: There came a man, sent from God, whose name was John.
The same came as a witness, that he might testify about the light, that all might believe through him.
He was not the light, but was sent that he might testify about the light.
The true light that enlightens everyone was coming into the world.
He was in the world, and the world was made through him, and the world didn’t recognize him.
He came to his own, and those who were his own didn’t receive him.
But as many as received him, to them he gave the right to become God’s children, to those who believe in his name:
who were born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.
b: This passage tells us that God sent John the Baptist not to be the light, but to lead people to the light. People easily fix their attention on other people and lift them up, but John knew exactly who he was: he was not the light, only one who pointed to the light. His role reminds us that the One truly worthy of our gaze and our following is Jesus, not any person. When our focus is on Jesus, hearts line up and the direction is right.

The passage goes on to say that Jesus is the true light who enlightens everyone coming into the world. When the light shines, people see the truth about life and the real condition of their hearts, and the way of salvation is made plain. Yet although the world was made through Him, the world did not recognize Him; He came to His own, and His own people did not receive Him. This is the tragedy of the human heart: God Himself came to find us, but people rejected the light, the truth, and the life.

But the story does not end in rejection; it turns to overwhelming grace. Verse 12 says, “But as many as received him, to them he gave the right to become God’s children, to those who believe in his name.” This is not by bloodline, not by effort, and certainly not by human resolve, but because God Himself has given us new birth and made us His children.

Becoming a child of God means our identity is completely changed. We no longer belong to the world, no longer rely on ourselves, and are no longer held by sin and darkness. We have a heavenly identity, the life of the light, and the right of God's children. This is a brand-new beginning, a life born of God, a life in which Jesus lives in us.
q: Have you truly let Jesus become the light of your life? In everyday life, how do you live out your identity as a child of God?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for sending the true light into the world so that we can see hope in the darkness. Give us soft hearts that do not reject the light or the truth, but are willing to receive Jesus, so that we may truly live out our identity as Your children. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: The Word became flesh, and lived among us. We saw his glory, such glory as of the one and only Son of the Father, full of grace and truth.
John testified about him. He cried out, saying, “This was he of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me has surpassed me, for he was before me.’ ”
From his fullness we all received grace upon grace.
For the law was given through Moses. Grace and truth were realized through Jesus Christ.
No one has seen God at any time. The one and only Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has declared him.
b: “The Word became flesh” unveils the deepest mystery of God's plan of salvation. The eternal Word, who was with the Father and was God, put on a human body and entered our world. He chose to dwell among us, so that in His life, His expressions, His words, and His footsteps people could see the glory of the Father. He is not a distant God, but a Lord who is near, whom we can touch and meet.

The passage says that from His fullness we have “all received, and grace upon grace.” He does not give grace only once; He keeps adding to it, so that in every need we receive new strength. The law shows our shortcomings, but the grace Jesus brings lets us stand up again; the law lets us know what to do, but Jesus gives the power to live out the truth. His grace does not patch up the old life; it gives a new life, so that we live by Him and not by ourselves.

Finally, John tells us that no one has ever seen God; the only begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has declared Him. Jesus did not merely teach knowledge about God; He fully displayed God's heart before us. Do you want to know how God sees us? Look at how Jesus welcomed the weak. Do you want to know God's holiness? Look at how Jesus faced sin. Do you want to know God's love? Look at how Jesus gave Himself up and served. Jesus reveals the Father's heart to us, so that we no longer have to guess, but can know God by knowing Him.
q: What kind of grace do you most need to receive right now? How will the Lord add grace upon grace to your life today?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for making Jesus the Word made flesh, so that in Him we can see Your glory. May Your grace keep increasing, so that we do not rely on ourselves but live each day by Your power. As we come to know Jesus, help us to know Your heart more deeply. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: This is John’s testimony, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?”
He declared, and didn’t deny, but he declared, “I am not the Christ.”
They asked him, “What then? Are you Elijah?” He said, “I am not.” “Are you the prophet?” He answered, “No.”
They said therefore to him, “Who are you? Give us an answer to take back to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?”
He said, “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way of the Lord,’ as Isaiah the prophet said.”
b: This passage shows us John the Baptist's clear understanding of his own role. He was humble before God and honest before people. When the religious leaders asked him, “Who are you?” John immediately declared, “I am not the Christ.” He did not try to exalt himself, nor did he use God's name to gain status or applause. He knew his place: he was only the one preparing the way, not the way itself.

The leaders went on to ask whether he was Elijah or the great prophet who had been foretold, and John denied each of these. He refused to claim glory that was not his, and he refused to accept people's mistaken expectations. He would not draw people to himself, but wanted to bring them to God. This is the heart of the new self: not grasping for power, but willing to let go; not living for oneself, but for the Lord.

When they pressed him again, “Who are you, then?” John answered, “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way of the Lord.’” Quoting the prophecy of Isaiah, he pointed out that his one mission was to prepare people's hearts so that the Lord's way would be made straight. John knew that he was not the light, only a voice pointing to the light; he was not the Savior, only a vessel leading people to the Savior.

This reminds us that in serving, our true worth lies not in how high our position is, but in whether our focus is on the Lord. God can use a humble heart and can display His glory through us, as long as we are willing to stand in the right place before Him, not stealing His glory or taking His place as King.
q: In your service and daily life right now, which areas need your attitude adjusted again, so that you give the place to the Lord and let His way be made straight within you?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us humility, obedience, and faithfulness through John's life. Help us to know our place, not to exalt ourselves or grasp at positions that are not ours, but to make Your way straight, so that through us people may see Jesus more clearly. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: The ones who had been sent were from the Pharisees.
They asked him, “Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the prophet?”
John answered them, “I baptize in water, but among you stands one whom you don’t know.
He is the one who comes after me, who is preferred before me, whose sandal strap I’m not worthy to loosen.”
These things were done in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
b: Those who had been sent were from the Pharisees. They asked him, “Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the prophet?” John answered them, “I baptize in water, but among you stands one whom you don’t know. He is the one who comes after me, whose sandal strap I’m not worthy to loosen.” This testimony was given in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.

When the Pharisees saw John baptizing, they challenged him: “You are not the Christ, not Elijah, not the prophet, so by what right do you baptize?” This is a typical religious mindset, concerned with where authority comes from, whether the qualifications are sufficient, and whether the position is correct. They were used to measuring spiritual work by human standards, so they could not see the new thing God was doing, nor the work God was already doing among them.

John's answer, however, was rooted in deep humility. He said, “I baptize in water, but among you stands one whom you don’t know.” He was not defending himself; once again he pointed the focus to the One who truly matters. His baptism only prepared people's hearts, but the One who can truly change lives was Jesus, whom they did not yet know, though He was already present.

Then John said, “I’m not worthy to loosen His sandal strap.” In those days, untying sandals was the task of the lowliest servant, yet John considered himself unworthy even of that service to Jesus. This was not low self-esteem; it was the humility that wells up naturally after seeing God's true beauty. The more people know Christ, the more they understand His greatness; the closer they come to the light, the more they see their own limits. This is a life led by the Holy Spirit: not grasping power, not exalting oneself, but wholeheartedly letting the Lord's glory be revealed.

Finally, the passage records the setting: these things happened in Bethany beyond the Jordan. The place is not the point; the point is Jesus, who stood among the people yet was often overlooked. God's work is often like this: He is right among us, but if our eyes are on ourselves, on systems, or on circumstances, we easily miss what God is doing.
q: In daily life, where are you prone to “see people but not see Jesus”? Today, will you adjust your gaze and recognize the Lord who is already among you?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, help us not to fall into a religious way of seeing, nor to measure Your work by our own judgment, but to see humbly, obediently, and attentively that Jesus is among us. Like John, may we keep our focus on Your Son, so that Your glory, and not our self, is seen. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: The next day, he saw Jesus coming to him, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!
This is he of whom I said, ‘After me comes a man who is preferred before me, for he was before me.’
I didn’t know him, but for this reason I came baptizing in water: that he would be revealed to Israel.”
John testified, saying, “I have seen the Spirit descending like a dove out of heaven, and it remained on him.
I didn’t recognize him, but he who sent me to baptize in water said to me, ‘On whomever you will see the Spirit descending and remaining on him is he who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.’
I have seen, and have testified that this is the Son of God.”
b: The next day, John saw Jesus coming to him, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world! This is he of whom I said, ‘After me comes a man who is preferred before me, for he was before me.’ I didn’t know him, but for this reason I came baptizing in water: that he would be revealed to Israel.” John testified, saying, “I have seen the Spirit descending like a dove out of heaven, and it remained on him. I didn’t recognize him, but he who sent me to baptize in water said to me, ‘On whomever you will see the Spirit descending and remaining on him is he who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.’ I have seen, and have testified that this is the Son of God.”

At a time when crowds were seeking repentance, direction, and salvation, John pointed to Jesus and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!” Not look at him, not look at circumstances, not look at the religious system, but “look at Jesus.” He is the redemption God prepared, the fulfillment of the entire sacrificial system, the only One who can truly take away sin, tear down what separates us, and restore our connection with the Father. Humanity's greatest problem is sin, and the only answer is Christ.

John went on to say, “He was before me.” Although Jesus was younger than John in the flesh, He was “there first.” This shows that Jesus is no ordinary man and did not begin to exist at His birth, but is the One who has been with the Father from eternity. His coming was not a beginning but a revealing; He was not created, but the Word made flesh.

John also said twice, “I didn’t know him.” This does not mean he did not know Jesus as a person, but that he did not know Jesus' true identity. Only when the Holy Spirit Himself revealed it, letting him see the Spirit descend from heaven and remain on Jesus, was he sure that this was the One who baptizes in the Holy Spirit. People can never recognize Christ by their own analysis, but once the light of the Holy Spirit shines, the truth becomes clear; once the Holy Spirit guides, the heart can see who Jesus truly is.

In the end John said, “I have seen, and have testified that this is the Son of God.” He did not testify from feeling or guesswork, but from revelation that came from God. True faith is letting the Holy Spirit lead us to see Jesus and giving all the glory to Him alone.
q: What are your eyes fixed on today? Are they on circumstances, on yourself, or on Jesus, the “Lamb who takes away sin”? Will you turn your focus back to Him?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for letting us see that Jesus is the Lamb of God, our only salvation. May the Holy Spirit guide us every day, so that we do not rely on our own judgment but see His reality, His glory, and His salvation. May our eyes always be fixed on Your Son. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: Again, the next day, John was standing with two of his disciples,
and he looked at Jesus as he walked, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God!”
The two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus.
Jesus turned and saw them following, and said to them, “What are you looking for?” They said to him, “Rabbi” (which is to say, being interpreted, Teacher), “where are you staying?”
He said to them, “Come, and see.” They came and saw where he was staying, and they stayed with him that day. It was about the tenth hour.
b: Again, the next day, John was standing with two of his disciples, and he looked at Jesus as He walked, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God!” The two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus. Jesus turned and saw them following, and said to them, “What are you looking for?” They said to Him, “Rabbi” (which is to say, being interpreted, Teacher), “where are you staying?” He said to them, “Come, and see.” They came and saw where He was staying, and they stayed with Him that day. It was about the tenth hour.

For the third time John the Baptist pointed to Jesus, saying, “Behold, the Lamb of God!” He did not draw people to his own side, but led them to Christ. A person who truly belongs to God does not make others depend on himself, but helps them draw closer to the Lord, know the Lord, and follow the Lord. When the focus is on Jesus, people's lives are naturally drawn toward the light.

When the two disciples heard this, they immediately left John and followed Jesus. This was not betrayal; it was the beginning of maturity. The ultimate purpose of any spiritual teaching, shepherding, or leadership is not to make people attach themselves to a person, but to bring them to Jesus, so that they connect with the Lord personally and experience Him personally. A person's influence is only the beginning; walking with the Lord is the true path of life.

Jesus turned and asked them, “What are you looking for?” This is the question the Lord asks us today as well. He was not asking what they wanted to get, but asking about their hearts: What are you seeking? Whom do you truly long for? The two disciples did not answer that they wanted blessings or miracles, but said, “Where are you staying?” In other words: “We want to know You more deeply and more closely. We want to be with You.” This is the heart of a true disciple, longing for the Lord Himself rather than the things He gives.

Jesus' reply was, “Come, and see.” He did not give a lecture or a long explanation, but invited them to “come, see, and experience for yourselves.” Faith is not knowledge but relationship; it is not watching from a distance but living with Him. The two disciples stayed with the Lord that day, and the direction of their lives was changed completely from then on.
q: If Jesus asked you today, “What are you looking for?” how would your heart answer? Do you long for His blessings, or for Him?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for drawing us to Jesus. May our hearts not only want Your grace but long for You Yourself. May we respond to Your call, coming every day to see, to draw near, and to stay with You, so that our lives are renewed as we walk with You. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: One of the two who heard John and followed him was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.
He first found his own brother, Simon, and said to him, “We have found the Messiah!” (which is, being interpreted, Christ).
He brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him, and said, “You are Simon the son of Jonah. You shall be called Cephas” (which is by interpretation, Peter).
b: One of the two who heard John and followed Him was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother. He first found his own brother, Simon, and said to him, “We have found the Messiah!” (which is, being interpreted, Christ). He brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him, and said, “You are Simon the son of Jonah. You shall be called Cephas” (which is by interpretation, Peter).

In this passage we see the most beautiful way the gospel spreads: a person meets Jesus and brings the person closest to him to Jesus. Andrew was not the best known of the twelve apostles, nor a leader, but he did something of crucial importance: he brought Peter to the Lord, and Peter would later become a pillar of the church, influencing countless generations.

This reminds us that God often uses people who are unknown, with no stage and no spotlight, to accomplish the most important work of His kingdom. God does not look at appearance, background, or ability, but at a willing heart. Those who are willing to seek Him will meet Him; those who are willing to share Him will become a blessing. Every time we bring someone to Jesus, though it may seem ordinary, it can change a person's eternity and the destiny of countless others.

When Peter came to Jesus, the Lord's first words were not rebuke or command; He saw Peter's future and gave him a new name: “You shall be called Cephas,” which means “rock.” Jesus did not look at what Peter was then, but at what he would become in the Lord's hands. What He saw was destiny, calling, and future glory, not flaws and weakness.

Peter by nature was impulsive, changeable, and prone to stumble, but Jesus saw the man God would shape him into: steady, strong, and dependable. The Lord treats us the same way: He does not define us by our past, but reshapes us with His life, so that we become the new self He sees.
q: Is there a “Peter” in your life whom God is waiting for you to bring to Jesus? Today, will you become an “Andrew” through whom the gospel flows?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for allowing us to meet Jesus. We ask for willing hearts to bring people to You. Make us like Andrew, who saw the worth of every soul. Open our eyes also to see Your calling and destiny for our lives, so that in Your hands we become new people. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
